memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Initial assessment for low mood and fatigue.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Mr reports persistent sadness, loss of interest, low energy, and trouble sleeping for 3 months. Denies suicidal thoughts.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/82 mmHg, weight 78 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 27 (obese). Appearance subdued, psychomotor retardation mild.
IMPRESSION: Moderate depressive episode. Ordered fasting lipid profile, fasting blood sugar, TSH, vitamin B12, PHQ-9.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start sertraline 50 mg OD. Advise diet low in refined carbs, increase walking to 30 min daily. Return if worsening sadness, suicidal intent, chest pain, fever >39°C, or black stools. Flu vaccine offered; patient declined today.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Sertraline 50 mg tablet, take one tablet once daily after breakfast. Continue for 8 weeks, then review.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: PHQ-9 score 14 (moderate depression). TSH 2.1 mIU/L (0.4-4.0). Vitamin B12 320 pg/mL (200-900). Fasting cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L (<5.2 borderline). HDL 1.1 mmol/L (>1.0). Triglycerides 1.8 mmol/L (<1.7 slightly high). LDL 3.0 mmol/L (<2.6 high). Fasting glucose 6.1 mmol/L (3.9-5.5) – impaired fasting glucose.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up on antidepressant trial and metabolic concerns.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient says mood better, energy up, but reports mild nausea and daytime fatigue. Sleep improved.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/84 mmHg, weight 77.5 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 26.8 (obese). No tremor, abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: Partial response to sertraline; nausea likely drug‑related. Continue monitoring lipids and glucose.
ARRANGEMENTS: Switch to escitalopram 10 mg OD. Advise taking with food, report persistent nausea. Return if worsening depression, suicidal thoughts, severe nausea, chest pain, fever >39°C, or black stools. Flu vaccine not due yet.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Escitalopram 10 mg tablet, take one tablet each morning after breakfast. Continue for 8 weeks, then review.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: PHQ-9 score 9 (mild depression). TSH 2.0 mIU/L (0.4-4.0). Vitamin B12 310 pg/mL (200-900).

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Patient booked a review appointment for 2025-10-05 at 10:30 AM with Dr Priya Natarajan (D03) for chronic disease follow‑up.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Review after medication change and pre‑vaccination visit.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient feels mood stable, reports less nausea, but notes increased appetite and weight gain.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/86 mmHg, weight 80.2 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 27.7 (obese). Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly.
IMPRESSION: Escitalopram tolerated; weight gain noted. Ordered fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar as yearly review.
ARRANGEMENTS: Add mirtazapine 15 mg HS for sleep and appetite support. Counsel on balanced diet, limit sugary snacks, aim 150 min walk/week. Return if worsening depression, suicidal intent, marked sedation, chest pain, fever >39°C, or black stools. Influenza vaccine administered today (02‑Oct‑2025).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Mirtazapine 15 mg tablet, take one tablet at bedtime. Continue as needed, review in 4 weeks.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Winter check‑up for metabolic parameters and depression.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports steady mood, good sleep, but worries about rising weight and occasional abdominal discomfort.
EXAMINATION: BP 134/88 mmHg, weight 81.5 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 28.2 (obese). Abdomen mildly tender in epigastrium, no guarding.
IMPRESSION: Stable depressive symptoms on escitalopram + mirtazapine. Lipids show elevated LDL; fasting glucose unchanged.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current antidepressants. Reinforce low‑saturated‑fat diet, increase aerobic activity to 180 min/week. Return if new chest pain, dyspnea, fever >39°C, vomiting, or black stools.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting cholesterol 5.8 mmol/L (<5.2 desirable). HDL 1.0 mmol/L (>1.0). Triglycerides 2.0 mmol/L (<1.7). LDL 3.6 mmol/L (<2.6). Fasting glucose 6.2 mmol/L (3.9-5.5).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Annual review of depression and cardiovascular risk.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient says mood remains good, energy adequate, no side effects. Asks about flu shot for coming season.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/90 mmHg, weight 82.0 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 28.4 (obese). No edema, lungs clear.
IMPRESSION: Depression in remission (PHQ-9 4). Lipids still above target; glycemic status unchanged.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue escitalopram 10 mg OD and mirtazapine 15 mg HS. Advise Mediterranean‑style diet, aim 200 min brisk walk weekly. Return if worsening mood, suicidal thoughts, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or black stools. Influenza vaccine offered; patient will receive in October.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Final visit within study window – pre‑winter assessment.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports stable mood, good sleep, mild weight concern. No new symptoms.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/92 mmHg, weight 82.5 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 28.5 (obese). Abdomen soft, no masses.
IMPRESSION: Depression well controlled. Cardiovascular risk factors persist; discuss statin if LDL remains >3.5 after lifestyle.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current antidepressants. Reinforce diet and exercise plan. Return if new chest pain, dyspnea, fever >39°C, vomiting, or black stools. Influenza vaccine administered today (11‑Oct‑2026).
